overview.description: 21 Point Black Tile is a Hearts-style domino game using a double-six set: 21 penalty points per deal. Three or four players pass three tiles left; leader nominates suit each trick. Lowest total score wins.

history.origins: Hearts-style adaptation for double-six dominoes; 21 penalty points per deal (variant of 11 Point Black Tile family). Western domino trick-taking.
timeline: Described as a 21-point scoring variant of Eleven Point Black Tile in Frederick Berndt's The Domino Book.
history.cultural: Same family as 11 Point and 30 Point Black Tile.

nullReasons.evolution: No documented evolutionary changes; game emerged as a stable tradition.

setup.players: 3 or 4 (same as 11 Point Black Tile; hand size varies)
setup.dealing: Tiles dealt; each player passes 3 face-down to the left before play. First player chosen by drawing highest total from boneyard.

rules.objective: Avoid taking tricks containing penalty tiles; 21 points in penalties per deal. Lowest total score wins.
rules.gameplay: Leader plays a tile and nominates suit (0–6 or doubles). Others follow suit if possible; highest in led suit wins trick. Winner leads next. Same as 11 Point but penalty total is 21.
keyRules: 21 penalty points per deal; lowest wins

strategy.basic: Mark penalty tiles; moon shots more frequent than in Hearts. Use double-0: lead as blank to win trick, or as double to dump it if another double is out.
strategy.intermediate: Lead low blanks to force 0-0 onto others; beware helping a moon-shot. When passing, passing high/penalty tiles left helps neighbour's moon-shot—sometimes keep them.
strategy.advanced: Holding doubles and penalty tiles can defend against moon-shots. Penalty tiles can fall to other suits; hard to defend. Same family as 11 Point and 30 Point Black Tile.
tips: Paint penalty-suit pips a different color to spot them.
0-0 as blank wins the trick; as double can lose it.
Passing high tiles left may give neighbour a moon-shot.
Same Hearts-style strategy as 11 Point; 21 points in play.
